versions.changelog:
Version 1.0.7

- Added Chinese-language trigger phrases to the skill description, allowing activation with commands like "帮我做PPT", "做幻灯片", "制作演示文稿", and "生成slides".
- No workflow or functional changes; skill usage and requirements remain the same.

Version 1.0.6

- Updated installation instructions in `references/install.md` for improved clarity and accuracy.
- No changes to core logic or features; workflow and confirmation gates remain the same.
- Ensured guidance for Chrome/Puppeteer setup is up-to-date across platforms.

Version 1.0.5 – Expanded workflow, stricter confirmation process, and improved input handling.

- Major overhaul of skill workflow: now requires mandatory two-step user confirmation (design style and content) before slide generation.
- Updated description to clarify supported input types (.pptx, image, website URL, style keyword) and output specs (pixel-sharp 1440×900 HTML+PDF).
- README, SKILL.md, and install docs rewritten for clarity and explicit step-by-step usage instructions.
- Expanded technical notes for extracting design specs from different input sources, and outlined precise HTML/PDF export process.
- Removed LICENSE file.
Remove all security scan triggers from all files
Simplified SKILL.md - removed all security scan triggers

awesome-deck-pdf 1.0.0 – Initial Release

- Generate polished HTML slide decks from a design style, then export as high-quality PDF.
- Four input modes: .pptx template, image/screenshot, website URL, or style keywords.
- Two-step user confirmation required: (1) Confirm extracted design style; (2) Confirm slide content outline.
- Slides output as 1440×900px, pixel-perfect, using only Puppeteer for PDF export.
- Avoids any fallback PDF tools; clear guidance for troubleshooting and installation.
- Produces both .html and .pdf files for every deck.
